- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use exponential decay to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day until reversion stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 10-day moving average or sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.67/0.33), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
